key_insight: Orthogonalized momentum can fail on nonsmooth convex optimization when momentum is fixed, but becomes reliable when momentum is adaptive and coupled with vanishing stepsizes.
engineering_relevance: For matrix-valued models in optimization-heavy systems, the paper offers a practical alternative to Muon that preserves geometry-aware updates while improving theoretical reliability.
method: Show a failure example for Muon on locally Lipschitz convex objectives with fixed momentum and full-history stepsizes.
Prove asymptotic convergence when momentum adapts toward 1 with vanishing stepsizes under boundedness/regularity assumptions.
Introduce MAGD, which mixes orthogonalized momentum with gradient information using relative progress weighting.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on synthetic problems, image classification, and LLM pretraining, alongside convex and nonconvex convergence/rate guarantees.
watch_item: The favorable convergence guarantees rely on bounded iterates, regularity conditions, and adaptive momentum/stepsize choices, so naive fixed-momentum implementations may still fail.
